body:
**requirements**

  * V2.1.1 Verify that passwords are at least 12 characters in length.
  * V2.3.1 Verify system generated initial passwords or activation codes SHOULD be securely randomly generated, SHOULD be at least 6 characters long, and MAY contain letters and numbers.

**problem**
If activation code does not have relatively short expires time, we should consider it as passwords and in this case requirements for password/code in V2.3.1 and V2.1.1 are different (in conflict)

**recommendation**
  * a) add requirement "expires time for actication code" to V2.3.*
  * b) increase password/code length requirement in V2.3.1

comments.body:
Initial activation passwords are essentially one time passwords. NIST chooses 6 characters to allow for PIN numbers for this first login, like Apple's device authorization. I think I would be miffed if I had to type 12 numbers when I add a new device. 

Thoughts? Does this change your view?

I don't have anything against this 6 number length but without "expires time" and without clearly one-time-password explanations we need to look it as usual password. From this point I can see 2 directions (like written in initial recommendation):

  *  a) add expires time requirement for initial password + say it out clearly - you can use "initial password" only once. My experience from pen-test cases: if users are not forced to change their initial password, they will keep using it.
  * b) if it does not have extra requirement like expires time and OTP requirement, we need to consider as usual password (from attacker perspective)
I've made changes as per checkin fa169b4. Please review and re-open if I didn't get it right

title: Conflict between V2.1.1 and V2.3.1 OR missing requirement for activation code expires time
